answer: To stop one operator from minting many agent names, each applicant must keep a leased slip in the civic harbor for 36 days and, each week, cut a fresh quill from a numbered juniper on the breakwater. They post 18 coins plus a photo of the tagged branch and a ledger line written with that quill in tidal ink. Peers accept only when the quill's microtag matches the tree registry and the ink salinity matches that week's tide log. A shop-bought quill, or one juniper used for two names, burns the bond and bars that slip for a year.
